To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The functional RNA domain 3.2 in HCV RNA CRE region is involved in IRES-dependent translation.
the functional RNA domain 3BSL3.1 within the NS5A coding sequence influences HCV IRES-mediated translation.
the functional RNA domain 3BSL3.1 in the CRE region negatively influences HCV IRES activity and that the stem–loop motif 5BSL.3 in the 3′-UTR is the major partner for this process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional role of the CRE region in IRES-mediated translation and its potential involvement in the circularisation process.
the functional RNA domain 3.2 within NS5B coding region, which is involved in the IRES-mediated HCV translation.
the role of the 3′ untranslated region of the HCV genome in the regulation of translation of viral proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
domain 5BSR3.2 is a negative regulator of HCV translation and that the 3′CRE domain acts as a positive regulator of HCV replication.
the CRE region is a cis-acting element that negatively regulates HCV IRES-mediated translation, and that domain 5BSR3.2 is a functional RNA motif that is involved in this process.
the CRE region of the 3′-UTR negatively regulates the IRES-mediated translation in a time-dependent and domain 5BS3.2-dependent fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
domain 5BS3.2 is a functional RNA motif that influences the IRES-mediated translation by the recruitment and/or stabilisation of protein factors.
the 3′-terminal CRE region of the HCV genome is involved in IRES-mediated translation by interacting with the IRES domain IIId.
the CRE domain 5BSl3.2 has a role as an inhibitor of HCV translation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
domain 5BS L3.2 is a functional RNA domain that is involved in the regulation of HCV translation.
domain 5BSl3.2 in HCV is a functional RNA domain that influences the IRES activity.
the CRE element in the 3′ UTR is involved in the regulation of IRES-mediated translation of the HCV genome.
